newsitem.title: INDIA: France's Total plans $450 mln India gas terminal.
newsitem.headline: France's Total plans $450 mln India gas terminal.

text.p: French multinational energy giant Total plans to build a liquefied natural gas (LNG) receiving terminal in southern India that could cost as much as $450 million, a company official said on Tuesday.

"We are presently carrying out feasibility studies," said Dominique Venet, Total's vice-president for business development in its gas division. "We estimate it will require an investment of about $350 million to $450 million in India."
Venet was speaking to Reuters on the sidelines of a two-day international conference on Indian oil and gas which began in the capital on Tuesday.
"Total believes not only that LNG is needed in India but that it is possible," Venet said.
He said India's natural gas demand was a little over 60 million tonnes per year in 1997 and that he expected it to rise to about 75 million tonnes annually by 2002.
Venet said Total had formed a 50:50 joint venture with India's state-run Hindustan Petroleum Corp Ltd (HPCL) to build the receiving terminal and a 2,000 MW power plant alongside.
"We are trying to decide the minimum threshold right now," he said. "That works out to about two million tonnes."
Venet emphasised that the India project cost was only one-ninth of the firm's total investment in the venture.
Typically, a project of this nature takes five years to complete, but Venet said Total was keeping its fingers crossed.
"We won't feel completely stable unless the required framework is in place, unless the state electricity boards can be settled."

Most of India's state-run electricity boards have been making losses for years. They are the principal clients of private power producers. If they could not pay their bills, Venet said, financing would prove very difficult.

Venet welcomed plans announced at the conference by the top civil servant in India's petroleum and natural gas ministry to frame laws setting up regulatory bodies in India's energy sector. "It's very positive, very positive," he said.
